clips.text_zh: biz有人問：如果只可以揸一樣嘢10年，你揀BTC定黃金？我自己就揀BTC啦，起碼唔會俾政府冚。黃金太old school，prop firm嗰邊我都係trade緊BTC為主，btw今晚又輸少少，又係學費。
clips.text_en_b1: A 4chan /biz/ thread asks: if you could only hold one thing for the next 10 years, would you pick Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Some anons say BTC, some say gold. The thread is still going. Pick one and explain your reason.
clips.source_hint: Anon asks 10-year BTC vs gold debate

signal.rationale: Open debate thread, no actionable setup, just a 10-year hold question

clips.text_en_b2: A /biz/ thread poses a classic dilemma: if you could hold only a single asset for the next decade, would you go with Bitcoin or gold, and what justifies the choice? Replies are split down the middle, with BTC advocates citing government confiscation risk and gold defenders calling it the original safe haven. The thread is still active. State your pick and reasoning.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ thread has resurfaced the perennial dilemma: if you were permitted to hold only a single asset for the next decade, would your preference be Bitcoin or physical gold? Anons remain divided, though a substantial contingent argues that BTC's decentralised architecture insulates it from governmental seizure — a vulnerability they consider inherent to bullion, which they dismiss as an outdated store of value. The writer personally favours Bitcoin, noting that their prop firm book remains predominantly long BTC, even as another evening of trading losses is wryly classified as 'tuition'.
clips.text_en_c2: A /biz/ thread poses a disarmingly simple hypothetical: if one were permitted to hold only a single asset for the next decade, ought one to choose Bitcoin or gold, and upon what rationale? The board remains predictably bifurcated, with gold partisans invoking its millennia-long track record as an inflation hedge, while the BTC contingent counters that no central bank can debase it at will. The proposition under examination is less about returns, more about which narrative one finds more persuasive in an era of monetary debasement. Whichever side one takes, the deeper question concerns conviction rather than calculus.

clips.text_en_b1: A 4chan /biz/ thread titled HAPPENING claims oil $150 is about to be reality, linking a Jim Cramer tweet on X. Anons are split — some say drill more, some say demand is dead. The thread is going crazy. Cramer is a reverse indicator to many anons.
clips.source_hint: Anon posts Jim Cramer oil $150 tweet

signal.rationale: Cramer tweet implies oil squeeze to $150, anons treat Cramer as reverse signal so bid gold as hedge

clips.text_en_b2: A /biz/ thread titled HAPPENING insists oil at $150 is imminent, citing a Jim Cramer tweet on X. Anons are divided — some call for more drilling, others insist demand has collapsed. The thread is in total chaos. To many anons, Cramer has become a well-known reverse indicator, so his bullish call only fuels the bearish crowd.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ thread titled HAPPENING has cited a Jim Cramer tweet in asserting that oil at $150 per barrel is imminent, prompting considerable volatility in CFD positioning. The poster themselves has already been stopped out of their crude exposure, having concluded that CFDs — particularly in energy — are wholly unsuited to their temperament and capital base; the cumulative drawdown has, in colloquial terms, been substantial. Rather than reopen positions, they are sitting on their hands at the prop firm until conditions clarify. Cramer's call has historically functioned as a contrary indicator for many anons, which only intensifies the sardonic reception this particular prediction has received across the thread.
clips.text_en_c2: A /biz/ thread titled HAPPENING circulates a Jim Cramer tweet forecasting that crude will shortly breach the $150 threshold, and the resulting discourse has fractured into two camps. The first contends that incremental drilling capacity remains woefully insufficient to meet surging demand; the second maintains that a demand-saturated market will render such projections preposterous. To many anons, Cramer has long functioned as a reliable contrary indicator, meaning the call is, if anything, a bearish omen for crude. CFD traders in particular have absorbed punishing losses and now regard his commentary with the suspicion it deserves.

clips.text_zh: 今日返工跟Tommy去斜坡做condition survey，做GI report。望住factor of safety數字諗嘢——soil nailing嗰邊要check drain位同地下管線。考牌書我都未睇完，但今日現場學多過睇書，lol。
clips.text_en_b1: Slope investigation and condition surveys are my daily work. I do ground investigation reports, check drainage, underground utilities, and soil nailing. Today I checked a slope factor of safety and realised I learn more on site than in the FE book. Civil site work beats study.
clips.source_hint: Generic anon story about being stuck, parallels feeling trapped in cycle
clips.text_en_b2: Slope inspections and condition surveys make up most of my day. I prepare ground investigation reports, check drainage runs, locate underground utilities, and review soil nailing layouts. Today I worked through a slope factor of safety and realised something obvious: hands-on site exposure has taught me far more than the FE study book ever has.
clips.text_en_c1: Today's site assignment involved accompanying Tommy to a slope where we carried out a condition survey and compiled the corresponding ground investigation report. Much of the work revolved around scrutinising the factor of safety calculations while cross-referencing the soil nailing design against the actual drainage layout and underground utility corridors on site. Although the FE examination preparation books remain only partially read, the practical exposure to these variables — drainage geometries, pipe alignments, nail spacing tolerances — has proven considerably more instructive than textbook study alone could ever be.
clips.text_en_c2: Slope investigation and condition surveys constitute the bread and butter of my professional routine, a fact I find myself contemplating as I pore over the factor-of-safety computations from today's site visit. Ground investigation reports must reconcile disparate data streams: drainage profiles, the proximity of underground utilities, and the integrity of any soil nailing already in situ. The FE reference manuals remain half-read on my desk, yet another day's fieldwork has yielded lessons that no textbook chapter could replicate. There is something to be said, I think, for the pedagogy of mud underfoot.

clips.text_zh: 夜晚睇緊FE嗰個load path chapter，beam同column點樣傳力去foundation。RC同steel design兩邊approach完全唔同，但logic係一樣——由top force到ground，唔好skip step。Dr. An話考牌實考呢part。
clips.text_en_b1: Studying load path for the FE exam tonight. Beams transfer load to columns, columns to foundation. Reinforced concrete and steel design use different methods, but the logic is the same — force goes from top to ground, never skip a step. Check every joint.
clips.source_hint: Generic biz thread, repurposed for structural study voice
clips.text_en_b2: Tonight I'm working through the load path chapter for the FE exam, tracing how beams and columns channel forces down into the foundation. Although reinforced concrete and steel design rely on completely different methods, the underlying logic stays the same — load travels from roof to ground, and you must check every joint.
clips.text_en_c1: Tonight's revision session has centred on the load path chapter of the FE reference manual, which methodically traces how forces migrate from beams through columns and ultimately into the foundation system beneath. Although reinforced concrete and structural steel adopt markedly different design methodologies — capacity hierarchies differ, connection detailing diverges — the underlying logic remains identical: every kilonewton must be accounted for, from the roof diaphragm to the soil bearing stratum. Dr An has repeatedly emphasised that this section is virtually guaranteed to appear on the examination, hence the reluctance to skip any intermediate step or joint verification.
clips.text_en_c2: The load path chapter of the FE reference has commandeered my evening, and for good reason: it is the conceptual backbone upon which every subsequent structural analysis rests. Beams transfer their tributary loads to columns; columns, in turn, convey accumulated forces down to the foundation; and the foundation ultimately delivers those forces to the earth. Reinforced concrete and steel design diverge markedly in their detailing conventions, yet the underlying load-path logic remains identical, which is to say that every joint warrants rigorous scrutiny. Dr. An has intimated, not without authority, that this material is examination-grade.

clips.text_zh: g/ 有人post：Grok最新update之後廢咗。以前Grok至少夠edgy，唔似ChatGPT咁答啲公關嘢，而家連個tone都變晒。X platform越搞越爛，Musk點搞架。AI仲話取代我哋藍領？先搞掂自己個product啦。
clips.text_en_b1: A 4chan /g/ thread says Grok sucks now. After the recent update, there's literally no point in Grok existing. The whole point was that it would do things other AI was afraid to do and answer edgy questions. Now it just answers like a redditor, an even shittier ChatGPT.
clips.source_hint: Anon complains Grok lost its edge after update
clips.text_en_b2: A /g/ thread complains that Grok has been completely ruined by the latest update. Its whole appeal was that it answered edgy questions other AIs refused to touch, rather than spitting out corporate PR like ChatGPT. Now it sounds like a polished reddit reply. The X platform keeps getting worse, and Musk's direction is baffling.
clips.text_en_c1: A /g/ thread has widely condemned the latest Grok update as effectively neutrally. Whereas the model once prided itself on a certain unfiltered candour — answering questions that competing platforms such as ChatGPT would have declined on PR or safety grounds — it now apparently parrots the same sanitised, evasive register that users had specifically sought to avoid. The poster contrasts this regression with what they perceive as the broader deterioration of the X platform under Musk's stewardship. They further deride the more grandiose AI narratives suggesting imminent displacement of blue-collar workers, arguing that if frontier labs cannot even maintain product coherence, such prognostications warrant considerable scepticism from anyone paying…
clips.text_en_c2: A /g/ thread laments the precipitous decline of Grok following its latest update, arguing that whatever erstwhile appeal the model possessed has evaporated entirely. Its initial selling point, after all, was a willingness to venture where ChatGPT would not: the unvarnished response, the refusal to retreat into corporate-approved equivocation. Now, however, it answers like a particularly tepid Reddit commentator, which is to say it has become a strictly inferior simulacrum of its rivals. The broader trajectory of the X platform invites analogous skepticism, and one wonders whether its proprietor might first attend to the coherence of his product before prognosticating about artificial general intelligence.

clips.text_zh: pol有人吹中國做到2nm，仲話冇用EVL機都得。我就諗，TSM同ASML嗰邊點頂。如果真係work，NVDA都冇得炒。返HK最大鑊係成日睇到呢啲吹水文，真假都唔知，lol。
clips.text_en_b1: A 4chan /pol/ thread screams CHINA HAS REACHED 2NM WITHOUT EVEN USING EUV. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO COMPETE WITH THE CHINESE SUPERMAN. Anons are split between cope and genuine worry about the foundry supply chain. TSMC and ASML are named.
clips.source_hint: Anon claims China hit 2nm without EUV
clips.text_en_b2: A /pol/ thread claims China has hit 2nm manufacturing without EUV machinery, declaring the West simply cannot compete with Chinese supremacy. Anons are torn between outright dismissal and genuine concern over the foundry supply chain, with TSMC and ASML singled out as the biggest losers if any of it turns out to be true.
clips.text_en_c1: A /pol/ thread has circulated claims that Chinese fabs have achieved 2nm process nodes without any reliance on ASML's EUV lithography platforms — assertions that, if substantiated, would constitute a genuine paradigm shift for the foundry supply chain. Sceptics within the thread dismiss such pronouncements as cope or outright fabrication, while others express genuine concern regarding the strategic implications for TSMC's market dominance and ASML's technological moat. Should the technology prove viable, the ramifications for NVDA's AI-driven valuation thesis would be considerable.
clips.text_en_c2: A /pol/ thread triumphantly proclaims that China has achieved 2nm fabrication without recourse to ASML's vaunted EUV lithography, a feat whose implications, if genuine, would be nothing short of seismic for the foundry supply chain. TSMC and ASML are duly named as the inevitable casualties, while NVIDIA's valuation is presumed to deflate in sympathy. The response bifurcates along predictable lines: some treat the claim as unalloyed cope, others discern genuine cause for disquiet. Living in Hong Kong, one encounters such triumphalist dispatches with weary regularity, never quite certain where technological reportage ends and partisan mythology begins.

clips.text_zh: fit有人問：80kg lean bulk完係咪應該即刻cut？佢2025年83kg肥，cut到65kg skinnyfat，之後反彈到80kg，flat bench 1 plate。睇到我好有共鳴，肥仔信都係咁，bulk完又cut，cycle到癲。我自己都諗住cut。
clips.text_en_b1: A 4chan /fit/ anon asks how to know when he has bulked enough to cut and escape skinnyfat. In May 2025 he was 83kg fat with almost no muscle, cut to 65kg skinnyfat by April 2026, could barely bench the 20kg bar, lean bulked back to 80kg now. Flat bench 3x8 1 plate.
clips.text_en_b2: A /fit/ anon asks how to tell when a lean bulk is truly finished so he can finally cut and escape skinnyfat for good. In May 2025 he sat at 83kg and overweight, slashed to a flat 65kg skinnyfat by April 2026, barely pressing the empty 20kg bar, then lean bulked back up to 80kg. Flat bench now sits at 3x8 with one plate.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ thread raises the recurring bulk-versus-cut dilemma: at roughly 80kg following a lean bulk, when does one actually transition into a cut to escape the notorious skinnyfat plateau? The poster's own trajectory illustrates the frustration — they began 2025 at 83kg with minimal muscle, cut aggressively to a gaunt 65kg by April 2026, rebounded to 80kg, and can currently press only a single plate for a flat bench set of three by eight. This cycle of depletion, metabolic adaptation, and subsequent regain resonates deeply with the wider former-fat community, for whom perpetual bulking and cutting has become something of a Sisyphean ordeal.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ anon solicits counsel on determining when a lean bulk has yielded sufficient muscle to justify a cut, a query that resonates with unsettling familiarity. His trajectory reads like a cautionary parable: in May 2025 he tipped the scales at 83kg with negligible muscularity; by April 2026 he had whittled himself down to a gaunt 65kg, barely able to press the unladen 20kg bar; a subsequent bulk has restored him to 80kg, where he now bench-presses a single plate for a modest three sets of eight. The eternal bulk-and-cut cycle, it seems, is the ineluctable condition of the naturally slender trainee.
